````md
# Highlight issues/milestones that are near, but not at, their deadline

## Context

Upstream issue: [CSCI-435-SE/gitea#3](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/3).

Today a due date is rendered in exactly two states: normal, or red once the deadline
has passed (`IsOverdue` → `tw-text-red`). There is no visual signal that a deadline is
*approaching*, so a user has to read every date to notice that something is due
tomorrow. The goal is a third, intermediate state — "due soon" — for open items whose
deadline falls within the next 72 hours, rendered in the theme's warning color.

Two adjacent problems surfaced during exploration and are in scope:

1. **Accessibility.** Three of the five due-date render sites convey overdue status by
   color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). Gitea's shipped colorblind themes
   (`theme-gitea-*-protanopia-deuteranopia.css`, `*-tritanopia.css`) only remap
   `--color-diff-*`; they inherit `--color-red` and the warning colors unchanged. So the
   new red-vs-warning distinction is *invisible* to a red-green colorblind user unless
   the color is paired with a text label. Every colored due date therefore gets a
   tooltip.
2. **A latent bug.** [milestone_issues.tmpl:34,39](templates/repo/issue/milestone_issues.tmpl#L34-L39)
   reads `.IsClosed` / `.IsOverdue` off the page context instead of `.Milestone`.
   `MilestoneIssuesAndPulls` ([milestone.go:260-261](routers/web/repo/milestone.go#L260-L261))
   only sets `ctx.Data["Milestone"]`, so both are a missing-key lookup on a map — they
   silently evaluate false and an overdue milestone never turns red on that page.

## Design decisions (confirmed with user)

- Color: **`tw-text-warning-text`** (`--color-warning-text`: `#9a6700` light / `#d29922`
  dark) — the variable Gitea designs for readable warning text, already used in
  [severity-colors.tmpl:96](templates/devtest/severity-colors.tmpl#L96).
- Threshold: a **fixed Go constant**, not an `app.ini` setting.
- Include both the tooltip accessibility fix and the `milestone_issues.tmpl` bug fix.

**No CSS or Tailwind changes are needed.** [tailwind.config.ts:45-55](tailwind.config.ts#L45-L55)
generates color utilities from every `--color-*` var declared under `:root` in the two
base theme files, so `tw-text-warning-text` already exists.

## Backend

The two models have deliberately different shapes — `Issue.IsOverdue()` is a method,
`Milestone.IsOverdue` is a field computed in XORM's `AfterLoad` hook. Keep that shape and
share one unexported helper so the semantics can't drift.

### 1. Shared helper — [models/issues/issue.go](models/issues/issue.go), beside `IsOverdue` (line 136)

```go
// nearDueDuration is how long before its deadline an open issue or milestone is
// considered "due soon". Deadlines are stored at 23:59:59 local time
// (routers/common/deadline.go), so this covers roughly the next three calendar days.
const nearDueDuration = 72 * time.Hour

// isNearDue reports whether an open item's deadline is approaching but not yet passed.
// It is mutually exclusive with the overdue check: a passed deadline is overdue, not near.
func isNearDue(deadlineUnix timeutil.TimeStamp, isClosed bool) bool {
	if deadlineUnix == 0 || isClosed {
		return false
	}
	now := timeutil.TimeStampNow()
	return now < deadlineUnix && deadlineUnix <= now.AddDuration(nearDueDuration)
}
```

Semantics: no deadline → false; closed → false; already overdue → false (the `now <
deadlineUnix` guard makes it mutually exclusive with `IsOverdue`, so nothing can be both
red and warning-colored); far future → false. `timeutil.AddDuration` already exists
([timestamp.go:47](modules/timeutil/timestamp.go#L47)).

Note `Issue.IsOverdue()` has no zero-deadline guard of its own — every template guards
with `{{if ne .DeadlineUnix 0}}` first. `isNearDue` guards internally; leave `IsOverdue`
as-is to avoid changing existing behavior.

### 2. `Issue.IsNearDue()` — [models/issues/issue.go](models/issues/issue.go)

```go
// IsNearDue checks if the issue is due soon
func (issue *Issue) IsNearDue() bool {
	return isNearDue(issue.DeadlineUnix, issue.IsClosed)
}
```

This automatically covers pull requests too, since PRs render through the same `Issue`
struct and the same shared list template.

### 3. `Milestone.IsNearDue` — [models/issues/milestone.go](models/issues/milestone.go)

Add the field next to `IsOverdue` (line 59):

```go
	IsOverdue       bool `xorm:"-"`
	IsNearDue       bool `xorm:"-"`
```

and set it at the end of `AfterLoad` (after the existing `if m.IsClosed` block, ~line 97).
The early `if m.DeadlineUnix == 0 { return }` guard at line 89 already leaves it false
for milestones with no deadline:

```go
	m.IsNearDue = isNearDue(m.DeadlineUnix, m.IsClosed)
```

## Templates

Five sites, all found via `grep -rn "IsOverdue" templates/`. The pattern is the same
everywhere — extend the existing two-state `{{if .IsOverdue}}` into a three-state
`{{if}}/{{else if}}` chain for the class, and attach a matching tooltip. Use an explicit
`if/else if` chain rather than `Iif`, which only takes two branches
([helper.go:169](modules/templates/helper.go#L169)).

`data-tooltip-content` is the right accessibility hook: [tippy.ts:124-135](web_src/js/modules/tippy.ts#L124-L135)
````

## Plan: "Due soon" (72h) orange state for issues & milestones

### 1. Backend design

**Naming:** `IsDueSoon` (method on `Issue`, `xorm:"-"` field on `Milestone`). It reads as the UI label ("Due soon") and pairs cleanly with `IsOverdue`. Both are reached as `.IsDueSoon` from templates — Go templates auto-invoke zero-arg methods, so the method/field shape difference is invisible to the 5 call sites. That's the key consistency lever: keep the existing per-model idiom, unify the *logic* in a helper, not the *shape*.

**New file `/workspaces/gitea/models/issues/deadline.go`** (package `issues`, next to both models, discoverable name):

```go
// Copyright 2025 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues

import (
	"time"

	"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"
)

// DueSoonDuration is the window before a deadline in which an open issue,
// pull request or milestone is considered "due soon".
const DueSoonDuration = 72 * time.Hour

// calcDeadlineStatus computes the overdue / due-soon state shared by Issue and Milestone.
// The two states are mutually exclusive: an overdue item is never "due soon".
func calcDeadlineStatus(deadlineUnix timeutil.TimeStamp, isClosed bool, closedUnix timeutil.TimeStamp) (isOverdue, isDueSoon bool) {
	if deadlineUnix == 0 {
		return false, false
	}
	if isClosed {
		return closedUnix >= deadlineUnix, false
	}
	now := timeutil.TimeStampNow()
	if now >= deadlineUnix {
		return true, false
	}
	return false, deadlineUnix <= now.AddDuration(DueSoonDuration)
}
```

**`/workspaces/gitea/models/issues/issue.go` (replace lines 136-142):**

```go
// IsOverdue checks if the issue is overdue
func (issue *Issue) IsOverdue() bool {
	isOverdue, _ := calcDeadlineStatus(issue.DeadlineUnix, issue.IsClosed, issue.ClosedUnix)
	return isOverdue
}

// IsDueSoon checks if the issue's deadline is within DueSoonDuration and not yet passed
func (issue *Issue) IsDueSoon() bool {
	_, isDueSoon := calcDeadlineStatus(issue.DeadlineUnix, issue.IsClosed, issue.ClosedUnix)
	return isDueSoon
}
```

Behaviour change to flag: `Issue.IsOverdue()` currently returns `true` for an open issue with `DeadlineUnix == 0` (`now >= 0`). The helper's zero-guard fixes that. I verified `IsOverdue` has **no Go callers** (only the 2 templates, both already guarded by `ne .DeadlineUnix 0` / `if .Issue.DeadlineUnix`), so no rendered output changes — it only makes the template guards non-load-bearing. Worth doing: without the guard, `IsDueSoon` would be `false` and `IsOverdue` `true` for deadline-less issues, which is nonsense any future caller would hit.

**`/workspaces/gitea/models/issues/milestone.go`** — add the field next to `IsOverdue` (line 59); `xorm:"-"` is mandatory or xorm will look for an `is_due_soon` column:

```go
	IsOverdue       bool `xorm:"-"`
	IsDueSoon       bool `xorm:"-"`
```

and rewrite `AfterLoad` (lines 87-98):

```go
func (m *Milestone) AfterLoad() {
	m.NumOpenIssues = m.NumIssues - m.NumClosedIssues
	if m.DeadlineUnix == 0 {
		return
	}
	m.DeadlineString = m.DeadlineUnix.FormatDate()
	m.IsOverdue, m.IsDueSoon = calcDeadlineStatus(m.DeadlineUnix, m.IsClosed, m.ClosedDateUnix)
}
```

The early `return` on `DeadlineUnix == 0` stays (it also guards `DeadlineString`), so the helper's own zero-guard is redundant there but harmless and keeps the helper safe for the Issue path.

**Explicitly out of scope:** `services/convert/issue.go` (`ToAPIMilestone`/`ToAPIIssue`). `IsDueSoon` is presentation state derived from "now"; putting it in the API payload would bake a server-render timestamp into a cacheable response. No `structs` change, no swagger regen.

### 2. Semantics

| case | `IsOverdue` | `IsDueSoon` |
|---|---|---|
| (a) no deadline (`DeadlineUnix == 0`) | false | false |
| (b) closed, closed before deadline | false | false |
| (b) closed, closed at/after deadline | true | false |
| (c) open, `now >= deadline` | **true** | **false** (overdue wins; red only) |
| open, `deadline - 72h <= now < deadline` | false | true |
| (d) open, `deadline > now + 72h` | false | false |

Precedence is enforced *in the helper*, not in the templates, so the "never both red and orange" invariant is unit-testable and can't be broken by a future call site. Closed items never go orange: a closed milestone/issue has nothing left to do, and the existing closed-item semantics are purely retrospective (`ClosedUnix >= DeadlineUnix`). Boundary is inclusive at both ends (`now >= deadline` → overdue; `deadline <= now+72h` → due soon), matching the existing `>=` convention.

### 3. Template edits (literal replacements)

Pattern: two template variables + an `if / else if` chain, set **before** the tag (html/template rejects `{{template}}` calls and some branching inside a tag's attribute context, so no shared partial for the attributes). `Iif` is rejected here because we need to pick *two* correlated values across *three* states — nested `Iif` would be unreadable. Variable reassignment with `=` is established in this codebase (`templates/repo/issue/view_title.tmpl:59`, `templates/admin/hook_new.tmpl:5`).

```go
func TestIssue_DeadlineStatus(t *testing.T) {
	now := time.Date(2024, 1, 10, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	defer timeutil.MockSet(now)()
	nowTS := timeutil.TimeStamp(now.Unix())

	cases := []struct {
		name            string
		issue           issues_model.Issue
		overdue, soon   bool
	}{
		{"no deadline", issues_model.Issue{}, false, false},
		{"far future", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(96 * time.Hour)}, false, false},
		{"just outside window", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(issues_model.DueSoonDuration).Add(1)}, false, false},
		{"exactly at window edge", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(issues_model.DueSoonDuration)}, false, true},
		{"inside window", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(time.Hour)}, false, true},
		{"deadline is now", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS}, true, false},
		{"overdue", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.Add(-1)}, true, false},
		{"closed in time, deadline soon", issues_model.Issue{IsClosed: true, ClosedUnix: nowTS.Add(-3600), DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(time.Hour)}, false, false},
		{"closed late", issues_model.Issue{IsClosed: true, ClosedUnix: nowTS, DeadlineUnix: nowTS.Add(-3600)}, true, false},
		{"closed, no deadline", issues_model.Issue{IsClosed: true, ClosedUnix: nowTS}, false, false},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			assert.Equal(t, c.overdue, c.issue.IsOverdue())
			assert.Equal(t, c.soon, c.issue.IsDueSoon())
			assert.False(t, c.issue.IsOverdue() && c.issue.IsDueSoon(), "states must be mutually exclusive")
		})
	}
}
```

Asserts: zero-deadline is neither state; the 72h boundary is inclusive and one second past it is not; overdue and due-soon are never simultaneously true; closed items are retrospective-only.

```go
func TestMilestone_DeadlineStatus(t *testing.T) {
	now := time.Date(2024, 1, 10, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	defer timeutil.MockSet(now)()
	nowTS := timeutil.TimeStamp(now.Unix())

	load := func(m *issues_model.Milestone) *issues_model.Milestone { m.AfterLoad(); return m }

	assert.False(t, load(&issues_model.Milestone{}).IsDueSoon)
	assert.False(t, load(&issues_model.Milestone{}).IsOverdue)
	assert.Empty(t, load(&issues_model.Milestone{}).DeadlineString)

	soon := load(&issues_model.Milestone{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(time.Hour)})
	assert.True(t, soon.IsDueSoon)
	assert.False(t, soon.IsOverdue)

	late := load(&issues_model.Milestone{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.Add(-1)})
	assert.True(t, late.IsOverdue)
	assert.False(t, late.IsDueSoon)

	far := load(&issues_model.Milestone{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(96 * time.Hour)})
	assert.False(t, far.IsOverdue)
	assert.False(t, far.IsDueSoon)

	closedInTime := load(&issues_model.Milestone{IsClosed: true, ClosedDateUnix: nowTS.Add(-3600), DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(time.Hour)})
	assert.False(t, closedInTime.IsOverdue)
	assert.False(t, closedInTime.IsDueSoon)
}
```

### 7b. 72h window vs. end-of-day normalization — the one real interaction

Deadlines entered via UI/API are pinned to 23:59:59 local (`ParseDeadlineDateToEndOfDay` / `ParseAPIDeadlineToEndOfDay` in `/workspaces/gitea/routers/common/deadline.go`). So for a deadline on day *D*, orange starts at `D 23:59:59 − 72h` = **`D-3` at 23:59:59**. Consequences:

- An item due *tomorrow* or *the day after* is orange for the whole day — good.
- An item due in 3 calendar days only turns orange at 23:59:59 that evening, i.e. it is orange for essentially the last 3 *whole* days. The window is "the next 3 days" with a one-second-into-the-evening lead-in, not "any date within 3 days". This is a real but minor UX wrinkle; if the intent is day-granularity, the alternative is comparing `DeadlineUnix.FormatDate()` against `now+2d` in `setting.DefaultUILocation`. I recommend **keeping the 72h duration** (matches the stated requirement, timezone-independent, trivially testable) and documenting the behaviour in the const comment.
- DST: adding 72h to a unix timestamp crosses a DST boundary as 72 wall-clock-minus-an-hour; at worst the flip moment moves by an hour once or twice a year. Not worth handling.
- Not all deadlines are end-of-day: migrated issues (`services/migrations/gitea_uploader.go:211`) and rows predating the normalization carry arbitrary times. The window logic is time-of-day agnostic, so those behave sensibly too.
- Sort orders, filters and the `due_date` API field are untouched — this is render-time only.

````md
# Highlight issues/milestones that are near, but not at, their deadline

## Context

Upstream issue: [CSCI-435-SE/gitea#3](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/3).

A due date currently renders in exactly two states: normal, or red once the deadline has
passed (`IsOverdue` → `tw-text-red`). There is no signal that a deadline is *approaching*,
so a user must read every date to notice something is due tomorrow. This adds a third,
intermediate state — "near due" — for open items whose deadline falls within the next
72 hours, rendered in the theme's warning color.

Two adjacent problems surfaced during exploration and are in scope by your decision:

1. **Accessibility.** Three of the five due-date render sites convey overdue status by
   color alone (WCAG 1.4.1 "Use of Color"). Gitea's colorblind themes
   (`theme-gitea-*-protanopia-deuteranopia.css`, `*-tritanopia.css`) only remap
   `--color-diff-*` and inherit the rest, so red vs. warning is *indistinguishable* to a
   red-green colorblind user unless paired with a text label. Every colored due date
   therefore gets a tooltip. `data-tooltip-content` is the right hook:
   [tippy.ts:124-135](web_src/js/modules/tippy.ts#L124-L135) mirrors it into `aria-label`,
   giving both a hover tooltip and a screen-reader label from one attribute.
2. **A latent bug.** [milestone_issues.tmpl:34,39](templates/repo/issue/milestone_issues.tmpl#L34-L39)
   reads `.IsClosed` / `.IsOverdue` off the page context instead of `.Milestone`.
   `MilestoneIssuesAndPulls` ([milestone.go:260-261](routers/web/repo/milestone.go#L260-L261))
   sets only `ctx.Data["Milestone"]`, so both are a missing-key lookup on a map: they
   silently evaluate false and an overdue milestone never turns red on that page. Without
   this fix the new state would be dead on that page too.

## Design decisions (confirmed)

- Color: **`tw-text-warning-text`** (`--color-warning-text`: `#9a6700` light / `#d29922`
  dark) — the variable Gitea designs for readable warning text, already in use at
  [severity-colors.tmpl:96](templates/devtest/severity-colors.tmpl#L96).
- Threshold: a **fixed Go constant**, not an `app.ini` setting.
- Include the tooltip accessibility fix and the `milestone_issues.tmpl` bug fix.

**No CSS or Tailwind changes.** [tailwind.config.ts:45-55](tailwind.config.ts#L45-L55)
generates color utilities from every `--color-*` var declared under `:root` in the two
base theme files, so `tw-text-warning-text` already resolves. Do not add variables or
safelist entries.

## Backend

`Issue.IsOverdue()` is a method; `Milestone.IsOverdue` is a field set by XORM's `AfterLoad`
hook. Keep each model's existing shape — Go templates auto-invoke zero-arg methods, so the
difference is invisible at the call sites — but unify the *logic* in one helper so the two
can't drift and the "never both red and warning" invariant is enforced in a single place.

### 1. New file `models/issues/deadline.go`

```go
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues

import (
	"time"

	"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"
)

// NearDueDuration is the window before a deadline in which an open issue, pull request
// or milestone counts as near due. Deadlines are pinned to 23:59:59 local time by
// routers/common/deadline.go, so in practice this covers the next three calendar days.
const NearDueDuration = 72 * time.Hour

// calcDeadlineStatus computes the overdue / near-due state shared by Issue and Milestone.
// The two are mutually exclusive: a passed deadline is overdue, never near due.
func calcDeadlineStatus(deadlineUnix timeutil.TimeStamp, isClosed bool, closedUnix timeutil.TimeStamp) (isOverdue, isNearDue bool) {
	if deadlineUnix == 0 {
		return false, false
	}
	if isClosed {
		return closedUnix >= deadlineUnix, false
	}
	now := timeutil.TimeStampNow()
	if now >= deadlineUnix {
		return true, false
	}
	return false, deadlineUnix <= now.AddDuration(NearDueDuration)
}
```

`timeutil.AddDuration` already exists ([timestamp.go:47](modules/timeutil/timestamp.go#L47)).

Semantics: no deadline → neither; closed → retrospective overdue only, never near due;
open and past deadline → overdue only; within 72h → near due; beyond → neither. Boundaries
are inclusive at both ends, matching the existing `>=` convention.

### 2. Rewire [models/issues/issue.go:136-142](models/issues/issue.go#L136-L142)

```go
// IsOverdue checks if the issue is overdue
func (issue *Issue) IsOverdue() bool {
	isOverdue, _ := calcDeadlineStatus(issue.DeadlineUnix, issue.IsClosed, issue.ClosedUnix)
	return isOverdue
}

// IsNearDue checks if the issue's deadline is approaching but has not passed
func (issue *Issue) IsNearDue() bool {
	_, isNearDue := calcDeadlineStatus(issue.DeadlineUnix, issue.IsClosed, issue.ClosedUnix)
	return isNearDue
}
```

**Deliberate behavior change to note in the PR:** today `Issue.IsOverdue()` returns `true`
for an open issue with no deadline (`now >= 0`). The helper's zero-guard fixes that. This
changes no rendered output — `IsOverdue` has no Go callers, and both templates already
guard on the deadline first — it just stops the guards being load-bearing. Worth doing,
since otherwise a deadline-less issue would report overdue *and* not near due.

### 3. Add to [models/issues/milestone.go](models/issues/milestone.go)

Field beside `IsOverdue` (line 59) — `xorm:"-"` is mandatory or XORM looks for an
`is_near_due` column:

```go
	IsOverdue       bool `xorm:"-"`
	IsNearDue       bool `xorm:"-"`
```

and collapse the branch in `AfterLoad` (lines 93-97) to one call:

```go
	m.IsOverdue, m.IsNearDue = calcDeadlineStatus(m.DeadlineUnix, m.IsClosed, m.ClosedDateUnix)
```

Keep the existing early `return` on `DeadlineUnix == 0` — it also guards `DeadlineString`.

**Out of scope:** `services/convert/`. Near-due is presentation state derived from "now";
putting it in an API payload would bake a render-time timestamp into a cacheable response.
No `modules/structs` change, no swagger regen.

## Templates

Five sites (`grep -rn "IsOverdue" templates/`). In each, set two template variables ahead
of the tag, then use them for the class and tooltip. This avoids repeating a three-branch
conditional twice per site and keeps branching out of attribute context. Variable
reassignment with `=` is established here (e.g. [view_title.tmpl:59](templates/repo/issue/view_title.tmpl#L59)).
`Iif` is unsuitable — it takes two branches ([helper.go:169](modules/templates/helper.go#L169))
and we need two correlated values across three states.

The shared shape:

```gotemplate
{{$dueClass := ""}}{{$dueTooltip := ""}}
{{if .IsOverdue}}
	{{$dueClass = "tw-text-red"}}{{$dueTooltip = ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.issues.due_date_overdue"}}
{{else if .IsNearDue}}
	{{$dueClass = "tw-text-warning-text"}}{{$dueTooltip = ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.issues.due_date_near"}}
{{end}}
<span class="due-date flex-text-inline {{$dueClass}}" {{if $dueTooltip}}data-tooltip-content="{{$dueTooltip}}"{{end}}>
```

Applied per site:

1. **[sidebar/due_date.tmpl:6](templates/repo/issue/sidebar/due_date.tmpl#L6)** — `.Issue.IsOverdue` /
   `.Issue.IsNearDue`. Already has an overdue tooltip; extend it.
2. **[shared/issuelist.tmpl:105-110](templates/shared/issuelist.tmpl#L105-L110)** — `.IsOverdue`
   on an `Issue`. Its tooltip is currently the unconditional generic `repo.issues.due_date`;
   initialize `$dueTooltip` to that so the default is preserved and only upgraded. This one
   template drives repo issue lists, dashboard issue lists, and the milestone issue list,
   and covers pull requests too since PRs render through the same `Issue` struct.
3. **[repo/issue/milestones.tmpl:59-63](templates/repo/issue/milestones.tmpl#L59-L63)** and
   **[user/dashboard/milestones.tmpl:118-122](templates/user/dashboard/milestones.tmpl#L118-L122)**
   — `.IsOverdue` on a `Milestone`. These blocks are byte-identical apart from indentation
   and **must be edited together**. Neither has a tooltip today; add one.
4. **[repo/issue/milestone_issues.tmpl:33-42](templates/repo/issue/milestone_issues.tmpl#L33-L42)**
   — qualify as `.Milestone.IsClosed` / `.Milestone.IsOverdue` / `.Milestone.IsNearDue`,
   fixing the context bug in the same lines this change already rewrites. Leave
   `$closedDate` on line 33 alone; it already uses `.Milestone.ClosedDateUnix`.

Also add the existing `due-date` class to the three milestone spans, which currently lack
it. It carries no CSS today (`grep -rn "due-date" web_src/` is empty) and is a pure

## Locale

Only `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` is hand-edited; all other locales are overwritten

```

## Tests

There is no existing coverage for `IsOverdue` at all, so this also establishes the
framework for deadline-state testing. Two layers, because they catch different failures.

### Layer 1 — unit tests (the logic)

New file **`models/issues/deadline_test.go`**, package `issues_test`, sitting beside
`deadline.go`. Table-driven against a mocked clock; no DB, so no
`unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()` — `Issue.IsNearDue` is a pure method and `AfterLoad` is an
ordinary exported method callable on a constructed struct. The established idiom is
`defer timeutil.MockSet(now)()` ([oauth2_test.go:43](models/auth/oauth2_test.go#L43)).

- **`TestIssueDeadlineStatus`** — one table covering: no deadline; far future; one second
  outside the 72h window; exactly at the window edge; inside the window; deadline exactly
  now; overdue; closed before deadline; closed after deadline; closed with no deadline.
  Each row asserts `IsOverdue()`, `IsNearDue()`, and that the two are never both true.
- **`TestMilestoneDeadlineStatus`** — builds `Milestone` values, calls `AfterLoad()`
  directly, asserts the `IsOverdue`/`IsNearDue` pair across the same cases, and that
  `DeadlineString` / `NumOpenIssues` still get set.

Do **not** build these on `models/fixtures/milestone.yml` — its `deadline_unix:
253370764800` (year 9999) is deliberately far-future and other tests depend on it.
`MockSet` is a process-global and explicitly not concurrency-safe, so neither test may call
`t.Parallel()`.

### Layer 2 — integration tests (the wiring)

Unit tests cannot catch the bug class this change is *also* fixing: a wrong field on a map
context renders empty instead of erroring, which is exactly how
`milestone_issues.tmpl` stayed broken. Five template edits referencing new fields is real
exposure, so assert on rendered HTML.

These use real wall-clock time — `MockSet` is a global and the test server runs
concurrently, so it must not be used here. Posting a deadline of *tomorrow* is always
inside the 72h window, and *yesterday* is always overdue, which makes the tests stable
without mocking.

Add to **`tests/integration/issue_test.go`**, next to the existing `TestUpdateIssueDeadline`
(line 659), which already demonstrates the POST-a-deadline pattern. Assert with
`NewHTMLParser` + `doc.Find(".due-date")` ([html_helper.go:38](tests/integration/html_helper.go#L38)),
checking `HasClass("tw-text-warning-text")` / `HasClass("tw-text-red")`:

- **`TestIssueDueDateHighlight`** — POST tomorrow's date to the `/deadline` route, GET the
  issue page, assert the sidebar due date carries the warning class and the "Due soon"
  tooltip; then POST yesterday's date and assert red plus the "Overdue" tooltip; then POST
  a date a month out and assert neither class is present.

Add to **`tests/integration/milestone_test.go`** (or `issue_milestone_test.go`, whichever
exists — otherwise a new file):

- **`TestMilestoneDueDateHighlight`** — create a milestone due tomorrow, then assert the
  warning class on both the repo milestone list (`/milestones`) and the milestone detail
  page (`/milestones/{id}`). The detail page is the regression check for the context-bug
  fix: additionally assert that a milestone with a *past* deadline renders `tw-text-red`
  there, which is impossible on `main` today.

Keep both under the sub-2s guidance in AGENTS.md — they are a handful of requests against
the existing fixture repo, no new fixtures needed.

### Not adding

No Playwright e2e test. The e2e suite is for browser-side behavior; this feature is
entirely server-rendered (`grep -rn "overdue" web_src/js/` is empty), so an e2e test would
duplicate the integration coverage at much higher cost.
````

by the Crowdin sync ([CONTRIBUTING.md:138-142](CONTRIBUTING.md#L138-L142)). Add one key

```json

```

One key serves all five sites. (The identifier is `IsNearDue` per your framing; the
user-facing string reads "Due soon".)

## Tests

There is no existing coverage for `IsOverdue` at all, so this also establishes the
framework for deadline-state testing. Two layers, because they catch different failures.

### Layer 1 — unit tests (the logic)

New file **`models/issues/deadline_test.go`**, package `issues_test`, sitting beside
`deadline.go`. Table-driven against a mocked clock; no DB, so no
`unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()` — `Issue.IsNearDue` is a pure method and `AfterLoad` is an
ordinary exported method callable on a constructed struct. The established idiom is
`defer timeutil.MockSet(now)()` ([oauth2_test.go:43](models/auth/oauth2_test.go#L43)).

- **`TestIssueDeadlineStatus`** — one table covering: no deadline; far future; one second
  outside the 72h window; exactly at the window edge; inside the window; deadline exactly
  now; overdue; closed before deadline; closed after deadline; closed with no deadline.
  Each row asserts `IsOverdue()`, `IsNearDue()`, and that the two are never both true.
- **`TestMilestoneDeadlineStatus`** — builds `Milestone` values, calls `AfterLoad()`
  directly, asserts the `IsOverdue`/`IsNearDue` pair across the same cases, and that
  `DeadlineString` / `NumOpenIssues` still get set.

Do **not** build these on `models/fixtures/milestone.yml` — its `deadline_unix:
253370764800` (year 9999) is deliberately far-future and other tests depend on it.
`MockSet` is a process-global and explicitly not concurrency-safe, so neither test may call
`t.Parallel()`.

### Layer 2 — integration tests (the wiring)

Unit tests cannot catch the bug class this change is *also* fixing: a wrong field on a map
context renders empty instead of erroring, which is exactly how
`milestone_issues.tmpl` stayed broken. Five template edits referencing new fields is real
exposure, so assert on rendered HTML.

These use real wall-clock time — `MockSet` is a global and the test server runs
concurrently, so it must not be used here. Posting a deadline of *tomorrow* is always
inside the 72h window, and *yesterday* is always overdue, which makes the tests stable
without mocking.

Add to **`tests/integration/issue_test.go`**, next to the existing `TestUpdateIssueDeadline`
(line 659), which already demonstrates the POST-a-deadline pattern. Assert with
`NewHTMLParser` + `doc.Find(".due-date")` ([html_helper.go:38](tests/integration/html_helper.go#L38)),
checking `HasClass("tw-text-warning-text")` / `HasClass("tw-text-red")`:

- **`TestIssueDueDateHighlight`** — POST tomorrow's date to the `/deadline` route, GET the
  issue page, assert the sidebar due date carries the warning class and the "Due soon"
  tooltip; then POST yesterday's date and assert red plus the "Overdue" tooltip; then POST
  a date a month out and assert neither class is present.

Add a new file **`tests/integration/milestone_test.go`**. Only `api_issue_milestone_test.go`
exists today — there is no web-route milestone integration test, so this establishes one:

- **`TestMilestoneDueDateHighlight`** — create a milestone due tomorrow, then assert the
  warning class on both the repo milestone list (`/milestones`) and the milestone detail
  page (`/milestones/{id}`). The detail page is the regression check for the context-bug
  fix: additionally assert that a milestone with a *past* deadline renders `tw-text-red`
  there, which is impossible on `main` today.

Keep both under the sub-2s guidance in AGENTS.md — they are a handful of requests against
the existing fixture repo, no new fixtures needed.

### Not adding

No Playwright e2e test. The e2e suite is for browser-side behavior; this feature is
entirely server-rendered (`grep -rn "overdue" web_src/js/` is empty), so an e2e test would
duplicate the integration coverage at much higher cost.

```go
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues

import (
	"time"

	"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"
)

// NearDueDuration is the window before a deadline in which an open issue, pull request
// or milestone counts as near due. Deadlines are pinned to 23:59:59 local time by
// routers/common/deadline.go, so in practice this covers the next three calendar days.
const NearDueDuration = 72 * time.Hour

// calcDeadlineStatus computes the overdue / near-due state shared by Issue and Milestone.
// The two are mutually exclusive: a passed deadline is overdue, never near due.
func calcDeadlineStatus(deadlineUnix timeutil.TimeStamp, isClosed bool, closedUnix timeutil.TimeStamp) (isOverdue, isNearDue bool) {
	if deadlineUnix == 0 {
		return false, false
	}
	if isClosed {
		return closedUnix >= deadlineUnix, false
	}
	now := timeutil.TimeStampNow()
	if now >= deadlineUnix {
		return true, false
	}
	return false, deadlineUnix <= now.AddDuration(NearDueDuration)
}

```

```go
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues_test

import (
	"testing"
	"time"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

func TestIssueDeadlineStatus(t *testing.T) {
	now := time.Date(2024, 1, 10, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	defer timeutil.MockSet(now)()
	nowTS := timeutil.TimeStamp(now.Unix())

	cases := []struct {
		name    string
		issue   issues_model.Issue
		overdue bool
		nearDue bool
	}{
		{"no deadline", issues_model.Issue{}, false, false},
		{"far future", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(96 * time.Hour)}, false, false},
		{"just outside window", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(issues_model.NearDueDuration).Add(1)}, false, false},
		{"exactly at window edge", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(issues_model.NearDueDuration)}, false, true},
		{"inside window", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(time.Hour)}, false, true},
		{"deadline is now", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS}, true, false},
		{"overdue", issues_model.Issue{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.Add(-1)}, true, false},
		{"closed before deadline", issues_model.Issue{IsClosed: true, ClosedUnix: nowTS.Add(-3600), DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(time.Hour)}, false, false},
		{"closed after deadline", issues_model.Issue{IsClosed: true, ClosedUnix: nowTS, DeadlineUnix: nowTS.Add(-3600)}, true, false},
		{"closed, no deadline", issues_model.Issue{IsClosed: true, ClosedUnix: nowTS}, false, false},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			assert.Equal(t, c.overdue, c.issue.IsOverdue())
			assert.Equal(t, c.nearDue, c.issue.IsNearDue())
			assert.False(t, c.issue.IsOverdue() && c.issue.IsNearDue(), "overdue and near-due must be mutually exclusive")
		})
	}
}

func TestMilestoneDeadlineStatus(t *testing.T) {
	now := time.Date(2024, 1, 10, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	defer timeutil.MockSet(now)()
	nowTS := timeutil.TimeStamp(now.Unix())

	load := func(m *issues_model.Milestone) *issues_model.Milestone {
		m.AfterLoad()
		return m
	}

	noDeadline := load(&issues_model.Milestone{})
	assert.False(t, noDeadline.IsOverdue)
	assert.False(t, noDeadline.IsNearDue)
	assert.Empty(t, noDeadline.DeadlineString)

	soon := load(&issues_model.Milestone{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(time.Hour)})
	assert.False(t, soon.IsOverdue)
	assert.True(t, soon.IsNearDue)
	assert.NotEmpty(t, soon.DeadlineString)

	overdue := load(&issues_model.Milestone{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.Add(-1)})
	assert.True(t, overdue.IsOverdue)
	assert.False(t, overdue.IsNearDue)

	far := load(&issues_model.Milestone{DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(96 * time.Hour)})
	assert.False(t, far.IsOverdue)
	assert.False(t, far.IsNearDue)

	closedInTime := load(&issues_model.Milestone{IsClosed: true, ClosedDateUnix: nowTS.Add(-3600), DeadlineUnix: nowTS.AddDuration(time.Hour)})
	assert.False(t, closedInTime.IsOverdue)
	assert.False(t, closedInTime.IsNearDue)

	closedLate := load(&issues_model.Milestone{IsClosed: true, ClosedDateUnix: nowTS, DeadlineUnix: nowTS.Add(-3600)})
	assert.True(t, closedLate.IsOverdue)
	assert.False(t, closedLate.IsNearDue)

	// NumOpenIssues is still computed as before.
	m := load(&issues_model.Milestone{NumIssues: 5, NumClosedIssues: 2})
	assert.Equal(t, 3, m.NumOpenIssues)
}

```

```text
func TestUpdateIssueDeadline(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	issueBefore := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 10})
	repoBefore := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: issueBefore.RepoID})
	owner := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: repoBefore.OwnerID})
	assert.NoError(t, issueBefore.LoadAttributes(t.Context()))
	assert.Equal(t, "2002-04-20", issueBefore.DeadlineUnix.FormatDate())
	assert.Equal(t, api.StateOpen, issueBefore.State())

	session := loginUser(t, owner.Name)
	urlStr := fmt.Sprintf("/%s/%s/issues/%d/deadline", owner.Name, repoBefore.Name, issueBefore.Index)

	req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", urlStr, map[string]string{"deadline": "2022-04-06"})
	session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
	issueAfter := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 10})
	assert.Equal(t, "2022-04-06", issueAfter.DeadlineUnix.FormatDate())

	req = NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", urlStr, map[string]string{"deadline": ""})
	session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
	issueAfter = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 10})
	assert.True(t, issueAfter.DeadlineUnix.IsZero())
}
```

```text
// Copyright 2017 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"io"
	"testing"

	"gitea.dev/modules/test"

	"github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

// HTMLDoc struct
type HTMLDoc struct {
	doc *goquery.Document
}

// NewHTMLParser parse html file
func NewHTMLParser(t testing.TB, body io.Reader) *HTMLDoc {
	t.Helper()
	doc, err := goquery.NewDocumentFromReader(body)
	assert.NoError(t, err)
	return &HTMLDoc{doc: doc}
}

// GetInputValueByName for get input value by name
func (doc *HTMLDoc) GetInputValueByName(name string) string {
	text, _ := doc.doc.Find(`input[name="` + name + `"]`).Attr("value")
	return text
}

// Find gets the descendants of each element in the current set of
// matched elements, filtered by a selector. It returns a new Selection
// object containing these matched elements.
func (doc *HTMLDoc) Find(selector string) *goquery.Selection {
	return doc.doc.Find(selector)
}
```

```text
func NewMilestonePost(ctx *context.Context) {
	form := web.GetForm(ctx).(*forms.CreateMilestoneForm)
	ctx.Data["Title"] = ctx.Tr("repo.milestones.new")
	ctx.Data["PageIsIssueList"] = true
	ctx.Data["PageIsMilestones"] = true

	if ctx.HasError() {
		ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplMilestoneNew)
		return
	}

	deadlineUnix, err := common.ParseDeadlineDateToEndOfDay(form.Deadline)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.Data["Err_Deadline"] = true
		ctx.RenderWithErrDeprecated(ctx.Tr("repo.milestones.invalid_due_date_format"), tplMilestoneNew, &form)
		return
	}

	if err := issues_model.NewMilestone(ctx, &issues_model.Milestone{
		RepoID:       ctx.Repo.Repository.ID,
		Name:         form.Title,
		Content:      form.Content,
		DeadlineUnix: deadlineUnix,
	}); err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("NewMilestone", err)
		return
	}

	ctx.Flash.Success(ctx.Tr("repo.milestones.create_success", form.Title))
```

```text
	assert.Equal(t, int64(1), int64(milestone.NumIssues))
```

```go
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"testing"
	"time"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/tests"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

// TestMilestoneDueDateHighlight also serves as the regression check for the
// milestone_issues.tmpl context bug fix: before that fix the detail page never
// rendered a milestone's due date in red, even when overdue.
func TestMilestoneDueDateHighlight(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	owner := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: repo.OwnerID})
	session := loginUser(t, owner.Name)

	createMilestone := func(t *testing.T, name, deadline string) int64 {
		req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/%s/%s/milestones/new", owner.Name, repo.Name), map[string]string{
			"title":    name,
			"deadline": deadline,
		})
		session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusSeeOther)
		milestone := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Milestone{RepoID: repo.ID, Name: name})
		return milestone.ID
	}

	assertDueDateClass := func(t *testing.T, selector string, id int64, wantClass string) {
		req := NewRequest(t, "GET", selector)
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
		dueDate := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body).Find(fmt.Sprintf(`[data-milestone-id="%d"] .due-date, .due-date`, id))
		if wantClass == "" {
			assert.False(t, dueDate.HasClass("tw-text-red"))
			assert.False(t, dueDate.HasClass("tw-text-warning-text"))
		} else {
			assert.True(t, dueDate.HasClass(wantClass))
		}
	}

	t.Run("near due on milestone list", func(t *testing.T) {
		tomorrow := time.Now().AddDate(0, 0, 1).Format("2006-01-02")
		id := createMilestone(t, "e2e-near-due-list", tomorrow)
		assertDueDateClass(t, fmt.Sprintf("/%s/%s/milestones", owner.Name, repo.Name), id, "tw-text-warning-text")
	})

	t.Run("overdue on milestone detail page", func(t *testing.T) {
		yesterday := time.Now().AddDate(0, 0, -1).Format("2006-01-02")
		id := createMilestone(t, "e2e-overdue-detail", yesterday)
		assertDueDateClass(t, fmt.Sprintf("/%s/%s/milestone/%d", owner.Name, repo.Name, id), id, "tw-text-red")
	})
}

```
